A1.justification: Both complete 40-page PDFs describe the same work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–I support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Sections 5–6 and Appendix I report original training and sampling experiments, including numerical-precision ablations and generation speed, perplexity and entropy measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results, including the training comparisons and sampling analyses in Appendix I.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–4 retain the same first-hitting recursion, uniform token selection, parallel decoding and higher-order variants. Model parameterizations and training objectives are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use OpenWebText for language modeling and text generation. No dataset, task, domain or distinct evaluation scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Figures 7 and 9 retain AR, SEDD Absorb and MDLM comparisons, including MDLM with and without caching. Comparator membership in the appendix experiments is also unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix H retains the data split, preprocessing, model configuration, training budget and sampling settings. Main sampling comparisons still use 64 generated samples; Table 2 still uses eight samples with 2048 steps.

E4.justification: The precision ablation, temperature trade-off, training investigations, higher-order sampler comparisons and generated-text examples are retained. Remark 5.1 newly references Appendix I.2.2, but its precision-robustness experiment already appears in v1.

E5.justification: Sample-averaging practices are unchanged. No repeated-run or seed disclosures, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty-estimation procedures are added or removed.

E6.justification: Numerical results, plotted curves and generated examples are unchanged. For example, Table 2 retains Gen PPL/entropy values of 31.24/5.17 for 32-bit, 126.11/5.66 for 64-bit and 28.64/5.12 for truncated 64-bit sampling.

T1.justification: Propositions 3.1, 3.2, 4.1 and 5.2 and their Appendix C proofs are unchanged. The appendix definitions and derivations are retained; added explanatory prose introduces no new formal result.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction refocus the criticism from superiority in generative perplexity to superiority in text generation, explicitly qualifying perplexity-only assessments through diversity loss. This is a limited refinement; the equivalence, 20-fold speedup and corrected performance-comparison claims remain.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 newly acknowledges that unchanged portions of a batch can be cached separately, with a possible parallel-efficiency cost. Section 5.3 explicitly connects unequal unmasking priorities to further entropy reduction. Existing text-domain limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Remark 5.1 removes the assertion that PyTorch's torch.multinomial implementation uses fixed 64-bit precision. This revises implementation documentation without reporting an experimental setting change; the algorithms, hardware, hyperparameters and pretrained-model access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: A new Section 3.1 footnote credits Ou et al. (2024) with the ELBO connection and distinguishes its time-agnostic network assumption from the present mixture-of-experts formulation. That work was already cited; the bibliography's membership is unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites affect the abstract, introduction and numerical-precision discussion, alongside added footnotes and a corrected Figure 12 cross-reference. The section and appendix organization remains intact.

P2.justification: Local layout adjustments compress Algorithm 1, reflow figure captions and reposition surrounding material; the conclusion starts on page 11. All figures and tables are retained with unchanged substantive contents.

improvement.justification: v3 explains the distinction between low perplexity and text quality more carefully, qualifies the caching argument, removes the blanket 64-bit implementation assertion and improves credit to Ou et al. These modest gains in precision and attribution improve the paper while its methods, proofs and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
